column1: # phrases.tsv — how each finding reads to a person.
# Titles recorded by the scans are precise and technical, and they are also the
# acknowledge keys in ~/.neptune/allow, so they never change for wording's sake.
# This table turns each one into a plain headline and a one-line context for
# the terminal, the text report, the HTML and the JSON. One table, one voice.
#   check     the check id the record carries
#   match     an ERE the title must match; the first matching row wins
#   suffix    an ERE removed from the END of the title first  (sub, once)
#   prefix    an ERE removed from the START of what is left  (sub, once)
#   headline  what the person reads; {s} is the text left after both removals
#   context   an optional second line; {s} works here too. When the finding
#             matches a known vendor, a vendor sentence replaces this line —
#             unless it starts with +, which marks a fact about this finding
#             ("only this Mac can reach it") that is kept beside the vendor.
# Keep the regexes to the subset BWK awk and Python agree on: no {n,m}, no \d,
# no lookaround. tests/test_render.py checks that the awk and python readings
# of every fixture title are identical, and that every check id has a row.
# Voice: say what the thing is, then what is off about it. Plain words.
